name: voice-mode-notice
opens_with: (shown at boot when audio is available)
notes: ENV: TuiApp::enter calls voice_mode_notice.show_if_available(audio_env.available, false), so on a host with a working recorder this overlay is VISIBLE FROM THE FIRST FRAME with zero keystrokes. Two consequences the runner must handle: this scenario only exists on audio-capable hosts, and on such hosts voice_mode_notice makes any_modal_open true for EVERY other scenario, which suppresses notification-banner. Note also that /voice REPLACES the notice with a fresh (invisible) state rather than dismissing it, so /voice is NOT a valid opener here. The assertion pins the notice label only, not a mode word: iter-541 made the line mode-aware ("Voice mode <state> to record"), because the old text hardcoded "available" and "startrecording" regardless of state and therefore lied while recording. Pinning the label keeps the assertion true across idle and recording.
